resources.string: Checking your Mini does not change its settings.
Choose how you want to use it.
Your Mini is already set up
You can check its details here. Changing how it works needs a reset first.
Your Mini is answering through the cable. You can check its details here. Turning its Wi-Fi back on needs a reset first.
It stopped answering. It may be restarting. This usually takes about 2 minutes.
We will check every 3 seconds for up to 3 minutes. If it still does not answer, we will show you how to reconnect.
We cannot reach it yet. Connect a cable or join its STARLINK Wi-Fi.
We could not check your Mini
The check took too long. We do not know your Mini’s settings yet. Keep it powered on and check again, or reconnect.
Waiting for the Mini to answer
This can take up to 1 minute. If it takes longer, try checking again.
This step comes in the next version. Your Mini is ready and waiting.
Plug a USB-C Ethernet adapter into your phone. Connect the adapter to the Mini’s cable port with an Ethernet cable.
Phone connected to a USB-C Ethernet adapter, then by a cable to the port on the Mini. The plug moves toward the phone.
Choose Join STARLINK below. When Android asks, choose STARLINK and tap Connect.
A phone asks to connect to the STARLINK network. The Connect button is at the bottom.
Choose STARLINK in Android’s message, then tap Connect. This can take up to 1 minute.
We could not join STARLINK. Turn on Wi-Fi and location in your phone settings. Check that the Mini is powered on, then try again or connect a cable.
Android needs permission to find and connect to your Mini. Tap Check again, or allow access in the phone settings.
Allow this app to connect to your Mini. Tap Check again to give permission.
Check mark: Mini already set up
Clock: waiting for the Mini to answer
Last readings from the Mini. Some details may have changed.
After a reset, the Mini uses 192.168.1.x. Changing this network address needs the official Starlink app.
With Wi-Fi off (bypass), one phone or laptop can use a direct cable connection and receive an internet address from Starlink. Only one device at a time can connect this way.
The Mini will have no Wi-Fi and no local network of its own. Its cable must go to a router.
To turn Wi-Fi back on, reset the Mini. Then choose “Wi-Fi on with password” in this app. Allow about 3 minutes.
Your phone will lose its Wi-Fi connection to the Mini. This is expected.
Checking the connection before you confirm. This usually takes less than a minute. No change has been sent. If the Mini does not answer, we will help you reconnect.
We are checking whether the Mini has switched off its Wi-Fi.
This usually takes less than 1 minute.
Keep the Mini powered on. If it takes longer, we will show you how to reconnect and check. We will not send the change again.
We could not fully check the change. Connect the cable as shown, then check again to make sure.
Connect the Mini’s Ethernet cable to your router’s internet port.
Look for WAN, Internet, or a globe symbol. This port is often a different colour.
Mini on the left. Its cable goes to the router’s highlighted Internet port on the right, labelled WAN or Internet.
This Mini is already set up
Reset the Mini first. Find the reset symbol on its back. Press until it clicks, then keep holding for 3 seconds.
Only the official Starlink app can change a Mini that is already set up. Reconnect to check its settings.
We could not check whether Wi-Fi turned off. Connect a cable or join the STARLINK Wi-Fi, then check again.
The change will not be sent again unless you choose it and confirm.
Keep the Mini powered on. Find the reset symbol on the back. Press until it clicks. Keep holding for 3 seconds.
Back of the Mini with the reset symbol circled. A finger presses and holds the symbol.
The light blinks quickly, then goes off. Release the button and wait about 2 minutes for the STARLINK Wi-Fi to appear.
Allow about 3 minutes in total. If STARLINK does not appear, check the power and connect a cable to check again.
The Mini is ready when this app says “Your Mini is ready”. Choose “Wi-Fi on with password” to turn Wi-Fi back on.
Name: enter at least %1$d character. Use up to %2$d English letters, numbers or spaces. Other letters and symbols may need a shorter name.
Shorten this name, or use English letters and numbers.
We could not join your new Wi-Fi to check it. Try again and tap Connect in Android’s message. This only checks the Mini; it does not send your choice again.
Password: %1$d–%2$d letters, numbers, spaces or standard keyboard symbols. Use English letters.
We made a strong password for you.
Use the same Wi-Fi as last time
Turn Wi-Fi on with a password?
The Mini will use this Wi-Fi name and your chosen password. Devices will need that password to join.
The Mini will restart. This usually takes 1–2 minutes. Keep it powered on.
If Android asks to connect, choose your new Wi-Fi name and tap Connect. This lets us check that the Mini is ready.
To choose again with this app, reset the Mini using the reset symbol on its back. Allow about 3 minutes.
The Mini may be restarting. We are waiting for it to answer and checking that your Wi-Fi needs a password.
This usually takes 1–2 minutes. If Android asks to connect, choose your new Wi-Fi name and tap Connect.
Keep the Mini powered on. We will check for up to 3 minutes. If it takes longer, we will show you how to reconnect. We will not send the change again.
We could not check whether your new Wi-Fi is ready. Connect a cable, or join your new Wi-Fi in phone settings, then check again. The Mini may have saved your choice already.
Wi-Fi code. Scan with another phone to join this Wi-Fi.
Other phones can scan this code with their camera to join.
Save this Wi-Fi on your phone
Android will ask you to save this Wi-Fi. Tap Save once. Your phone can then join it automatically when it is nearby.
Android will show a notification asking whether this app can suggest Wi-Fi. Allow it so your phone can join your Mini automatically when it is nearby.
If your phone does not join, choose your Wi-Fi name in phone settings. The password and code stay available here.
Wi-Fi saved on this phone. It can now join automatically. If it does not join, choose this Wi-Fi name in phone settings.
This Wi-Fi is already saved. Choose it in phone settings. If its old password is different, forget it there and try saving it again.
Wi-Fi was not saved on this phone. Tap Join on this phone to try again, or use the password and code below.
Look for Android’s Wi-Fi notification and allow this app’s suggestion. If your phone does not join, choose this Wi-Fi in phone settings.
Android could not save this Wi-Fi. Choose it in phone settings and use the password below. Other phones can still scan the code.
We could not remember this password safely. No change was sent. Try again, or go back and restart the app.
A phone asks to connect to the %1$s Wi-Fi. The Connect button is at the bottom.
We have not checked whether the Mini saved this Wi-Fi. Try joining with these details, or connect a cable and check again.
If nothing happens after a minute, close the phone’s connection message and try Join STARLINK again. Keep the phone close to the Mini.
Resetting removes the Mini’s saved Wi-Fi name and password. Everyone using it will lose their connection.
Back of the Mini. Its light blinks quickly, then stays off. An off light alone does not mean the Mini is ready.
Turn on Wi-Fi on your phone. Look for the name STARLINK. It does not need a password.
A drawn phone Wi-Fi list with the open network STARLINK marked by a Wi-Fi symbol. Choose this name.
Tap Join STARLINK below. In Android’s message, choose STARLINK and tap Connect.
Already joined? Tap Next to check.
We will check your Mini. When it says “Your Mini is ready”, choose “Wi-Fi off” or “Wi-Fi on with password”.
The Mini with a circular arrow: restarting. Keep its power connected while it starts again.
Set up Mini. Open the app to choose how to use your Mini.
